claim: RAG (Lewis et al., NeurIPS 2020): parametric models store factual knowledge but 'providing provenance for their decisions and updating their world knowledge remain open research problems' — supports the lesson's 'why retrieval instead of a bigger model' rationale

Instruction Hierarchy (Wallace et al., 2024): LLMs treat system prompts as the same priority as untrusted user/third-party text; proposes hierarchy (system > developer > user > tool) so conflicts resolve by privilege
Embedding inversion (Morris et al., EMNLP 2023): inversion = reconstructing full text from dense embeddings; 92% exact recovery of 32-token inputs; full names recovered from clinical-note embeddings

Canary methodology (Carlini et al., 'The Secret Sharer', USENIX Security 2019): randomly-chosen canary sequences inserted into training data; exposure metric measures memorization; extraction of secret sequences demonstrated

EU AI Act Art. 43: conformity assessment = provider demonstrates compliance via internal control (Annex VI) or notified-body assessment (Annex VII); Art. 65: 'systemic risk' = risk specific to high-impact capabilities of GPAI models; Art. 55: systemic-risk obligations (model evaluation incl. adversarial testing, risk mitigation, incident reporting, cybersecurity)

HF Transformers glossary: causal language modeling = pretraining task predicting the next word; pretraining uses a self-supervised objective ('reading the text and trying to predict the next word'); finetuning = transfer learning on a pretrained model

GitHub artifact attestations: Sigstore-based signed build provenance for CI artifacts; SLSA v1.0 Build Level 2; attestations must be verified to provide benefit ('Generating attestations alone doesn't provide any security benefit')

in-toto: framework to protect supply-chain integrity; project owner creates signed layout (steps + authorized functionaries); per-step signed link metadata records materials/products; verification checks links against layout
OpenSSF Scorecard: automated tool assessing security-health heuristics ('checks') of open-source projects, each scored 0-10; goals include helping consumers judge dependency risk
